title: Robust bistable vortex light bullets in graded-index multimode fibers
authors: Ashis Paul, Anuj P. Lara, Govind P. Agrawal, Samudra Roy
abstract: We explore theoretically the formation and evolution of spatiotemporal vortex bullets, pulses confined in both space and time while carrying orbital angular momentum, inside a graded-index multimode fiber. Through a two-fold approach, combining variational analysis with full numerical simulations, we establish the existence of a bistable vortex soliton family, characterized by distinct radial and azimuthal quantum numbers. These wave packets exhibit a Laguerre-Gaussian multi-ring topology in their spatiotemporal structure. We identify the experimental conditions necessary for the generation of such structured states of light. A stability analysis based on Vakhitov-Kolokolov criteria reveals an upper limit for the propagation constant, below which vortex bullets are found to be stable. Stationary and non-stationary dynamics of vortex bullets with different topological charges are analyzed fully, exploiting analytical techniques that are supported by full numerical simulations. These results enhance our understanding of self-trapped, spatiotemporal vortex solitons in a graded-index medium and may lead to potential applications in the area of classical and quantum information processing.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes the existence and stability of spatiotemporal vortex light bullets propagating in graded-index multimode fibers. By combining variational calculus with numerical methods, the authors prove the existence of a bistable family of these structured solitons. The findings suggest that these stable, high-order light structures have potential applications in classical and quantum information processing.
main_problem: The paper investigates the theoretical formation and evolution of spatiotemporal vortex light bullets (STOV bullets) within a graded-index multimode fiber.
main_result: The authors establish the existence of a bistable vortex soliton family, demonstrating that GRIN fibers can stabilize these structured light wave packets.
method: A two-fold approach combining variational analysis with full numerical simulations was used to solve the nonlinear Schrödinger equation.
model_or_system: The system models light propagation in a $	ext{GeO}_2$-doped silica GRIN fiber, governed by the (3+1)D Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation (NLSE). The vortex structure is characterized by an orbital angular momentum quantum number ($l$).
key_observables: Bistability, stability (via Vakhitov–Kolokolov criterion), and the spatiotemporal intensity profiles of the vortex bullets.
important_parameters: Topological charge ($l$), dimensionless GVD ($\delta^2$), nonlinear parameter ($\gamma$), and the fiber's refractive index profile parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes radial symmetry ($\Psi(ho, T) = \psi(ho, T) \exp(il\phi + i\mu Z)$) and utilizes the variational method as an approximation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically shows the STOV bullet, the refractive index profile, and dispersion characteristics. Figure 2 illustrates the spatio-temporal distributions and the energy dependence demonstrating bistability for different vortex modes.
paper_structure: The paper first sets up the physical model using the NLSE, then employs variational analysis to derive a reduced Lagrangian. This leads to finding closed-form solutions for the soliton parameters, demonstrating bistability, and finally analyzing the stability using the Vakhitov-Kolokolov criterion.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and nonlinear wave physics, as it predicts stable, structured light states (vortex solitons) that could be utilized in advanced quantum information processing applications.
